subject.title: [Feature]: Granular session visibility — split tools.sessions.visibility into per-capability knobs

question: Should OpenClaw add a per-capability `tools.sessions.visibility` object, or should send/read/list separation be solved through the existing A2A allowlist, per-agent visibility, or allowlist proposals instead?
rationale: This changes the cross-agent transcript privacy boundary and public config shape, and active related proposals overlap the same session authorization surface without a settled model.

options.title: Approve capability object
options.body: Adopt a backward-compatible object form for send/history/list/metadata after reconciling it with allowlist, per-agent, sandbox, and A2A semantics.

options.title: Use adjacent scoping models
options.body: Make per-agent A2A/session scoping or session-key allowlists canonical if maintainers decide they satisfy the send-without-read privacy goal more cleanly.

options.title: Defer until related PRs settle
options.body: Keep this issue as the canonical design question while adjacent PRs are reviewed, repaired, merged, or closed.

recommendation.title: Approve capability object
recommendation.body: Adopt a backward-compatible object form for send/history/list/metadata after reconciling it with allowlist, per-agent, sandbox, and A2A semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The current shared session-tool authorization and config boundary traces most clearly through Peter Steinberger’s security scoping and access-helper work.
